Jacobsen HA et al. are the authors of a pivotal 2022 validation study that underpins the epidemiological and technical foundation for monitoring Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) in Denmark. Their research is central to verifying the data quality of the Danish National Patient Registry ([[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]]), which serves as the primary source for patient inclusion in the national IBD database (DANIBD) [^src1] [^src2].

In 2022, the group published a population-based study from the North Denmark Region that investigated the validity of IBD diagnoses recorded in the national registry [^src1]. By comparing these national registrations against the regional IBD database [[gastrobio|GASTROBIO]], the authors demonstrated a highly reliable positive predictive value (PPV) [^src1]. Specifically, the study found a high PPV of 0.95 (95% CI, 0.95–0.96) for IBD diagnoses [^src2]. 

This validation is frequently cited in DANIBD annual reports to justify the use of action diagnoses from the national registry for identifying and including patients [^src2]. By confirming the high accuracy of these diagnostic codes, the work of Jacobsen HA et al. provides the necessary evidence to support the registry's coverage rates and the reliability of its quality indicators, such as those measuring colonoscopy rates for PSC/IBD comorbidities and the education of newly diagnosed patients [^src1] [^src2].
